* **Levels.** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of
 them a model accepts is `supportedReason
ingEfforts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that
model — do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and re
corded on the execution record, or refused with\n `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling\n tempe
rature.\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent
alone it pins its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model\n instead
of failing.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps
the case's existing selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved select
ion on a client `set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credenti
al field; an unknown key\n (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.\n* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
\n reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was n
ever applied, so\n writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored\n value is refused by the runne

r.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a
per-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinn
ed on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved sele
ction carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.\n\nThe SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same o
perations:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`send

modelSelection`) when there is none.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available

over the API
today (most exist in the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design — see [Authent
ication](#authentication))\n* Chat and conformance suites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourse

lf,
 then upload the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Disc

ord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) — it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **
path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **Duri
ng the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog
/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — are
considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable iden

tifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `sc
enario` is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the

noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/project
s/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/stu
dies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\
n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-r
uns/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` |
`.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs

/{swarmRunId}/insights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `

swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`g
et_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-depen

dent fields are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including
its old response\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undocu

mented on purpose — the spec is what a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of oper
ations kept their names through the rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,

`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — never both in
one request — until general availability.

###

Vocabulary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with
one string in it, and a client swit

ching on `"scenario"` has no second name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the

renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` |
`study` |\n| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`
, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scena

rio` | `study` |
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's c
ontract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spellin
g; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two

implementations can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **
separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may s

peak one
and not the other, so read
`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are
two blocks
— before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or\n`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one

you already hold.

Permalink resource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical k
eys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOP
ERATION rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.ap

iVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depen
ds on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-se
ssions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial g
rant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and
traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.\n\n| Method | Path
| Purpose |\n| - | - | - |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `pol
icy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake th
e session browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy w
ith a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat
